options.text: The triangles are congruent by ASA: two angles and the included side match.
The triangles are congruent from the equal included side alone.
The matching angles and included side come from first declaring the triangles congruent.
Two angles with no side given are enough for congruence here.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

teacher.key_rationale: ASA needs two angles and the included side; those are given. Side alone omits the angles. Declaring congruence first reverses the dependence. Angle-only data stretches beyond ASA.

stem: Qasim has $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$. He knows $\angle B=\angle E$, $\angle C=\angle F$, and side $BC=EF$ lies between those equal angles in each triangle.

part_answers.answer: Two equal angles and the included equal side BC=EF give ASA, so the triangles are congruent.
